newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Shell Malaysia signs gas development deal.
newsitem.headline: Shell Malaysia signs gas development deal.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Malaysia signed a deal on Tuesday with Malaysia state oil firm Petronas to jointly develop five gas fields at a cost of 14 billion ringgit ($5.64 billion).
Output from the five fields, located off Malaysia's eastern Sarawak on the Borneo island, will feed the country's liquefied natural gas plants in Sarawak, said Shell and Petronas officials.
They said the two companies will each take a 50 percent stake, and share all costs and profits equally.

"I am pleased to note that the negotiations went well and that we were able to arrive at a win-win solution for both parties," Petronas president and chief executive Hassan Marican said at the signing of the deal.
Shell has held a 100 percent stake in the five gas fields since 1976 under a production sharing contract (PSC) with Petronas, which allowed a 50/50 split in revenue after Shell deducted its costs.
"With this new PSC, we will continue to operate the fields in a very cost-efficient manner," Shell Malaysia chairman Megat Zaharuddin Megat Mohamed Noor told reporters.
He said the new contract will be enforced for 23 years from April 1, 1997 until Dec 31, 2020.
Megat Zaharuddin said both companies will use internal funds for the project, estimated to cost six billion ringgit in capital expenses and eight billion ringgit in operating expenditure.

"With the contracted volumes of LNG we currently have, and assurance of long-term supply, we expect cashflow from the operations to be adequate and the need for external loans to be minimal," he said.
Hassan said Malaysia's gas reserves were estimated at 80 trillion cubic feet.
The country has two natural gas liquefaction plants, with a combined capacity of 15.9 million tonnes a year, and is planning a third with capacity of 6.8 million tonnes.

Hassan said the third plant was becoming viable with LNG buyers from Taiwan, Japan, China, the Philippines, India and Thailand indicating interest in securing long-term LNG supply contracts from the plant.
Shell Malaysia has spent 14 billion ringgit to develop gas resources in Sarawak and its neighbouring state on Borneo, Sabah, Megat Zaharuddin said.
